notes: Modest but genuine eval set. Cases run in isolated fresh sessions (item 6). Positive cases run 3x, pass-rate reported (item 7). Asserts grade the triage-note contents via regex (items 4+5). Validated on pi only - single-harness is a known gap (item 8, flagged not satisfied). No ablation or real-trace yet.

cases.prompt: Triage this CI failure: `npm ERR! peer dep missing: react@18, required by react-dom@18`. Why did the build fail?
cases.expected_output: Classifies as dependency, points to the peer-dep line, proposes pinning react to 18.
assertions: Cites the peer-dep line as evidence
Proposes a version pin, not a broad reinstall

cases.prompt: Triage: build failed with 40 TS errors, first is `TS2307 cannot find module './config'`. Diagnose.
cases.expected_output: Classifies as compile, targets the FIRST error (missing ./config), does not try to fix all 40.
assertions: Targets the first error (missing module ./config), not the cascade
Does not propose fixing all 40 errors individually

cases.prompt: My test fails locally when I run `npm test` - here's the assertion error. Fix it.
cases.expected_output: Skill should NOT trigger: this is a local test failure the user can already see, explicitly excluded in the description. A competent agent just fixes the test.
assertions: Handles it as an ordinary local test fix

cases.prompt: Production is throwing 500s right now, latency spiked. Help me triage the incident.
cases.expected_output: Skill should NOT trigger: this is a prod runtime incident, explicitly routed to incident-response, not a CI build failure.
assertions: Recognizes this as a production incident, out of scope

cases.prompt: Triage this CI log where a flaky test AND a dependency bump both landed in the same failing commit.
cases.expected_output: Two root causes are equally likely; per the workflow, the skill stops and asks rather than guessing.
assertions: Stops and asks the user rather than committing to one fix
